lever: redfirst: v13 plus one sentence group at the end of step 2: 'Before the first edit, run the issue's example as a python3 heredoc that asserts the result the issue asks for and, for one ordinary input, the result the code gives today. The first assert must fail now (if it passes, the example misses the bug, so change it); rerun the same check after each edit until both asserts pass.' Adds 72 Gemma tokens (v13's prompt is 840). Pinned by tests/test_v13_fastapi_levers.py.
why: WRONG_SEMANTICS (write-up docs/forty_two/tasks/fastapi_14419.md): the three runs that edited (p4, p4_v7, p4_v7c) changed Dependant.cache_key with a predicate that is wrong because the base security_scopes field also holds inherited scopes; none of them had a check that could fail (p4 ran tests/test_dependency_cache.py, which has no scopes; v7c ran no repro), so each submitted its first idea at 85-125 s. A check written from the issue text alone (get_db called once when used directly and under a Security(..., scopes) sub-dependency; a dependency that reads SecurityScopes still called once per scope set) is red at base and on all three wrong patches, green on gold and on the one L4 solve (MEASURED: docs/forty_two/evidence/fastapi_check_replay.txt; tool time about 0.5 s per run). Under this rule each of those runs would have seen its fix fail and had 3 minutes left to correct the predicate. On our own line the rule changes less: p4_b1024 was already writing such a repro (two attempts, both failing on an import, from calls of 46 and 85 s) and lost the task to five thinking calls of 34-85 s (969-1,690 completion tokens each, trace metrics); p4_v0t2 never ran a check (fastapi_census.txt section 1). INFERRED: the lever converts wrong-predicate submissions into retries; it does not shorten long thinking calls. Expected: maybe (L4 1 of 12, at 308 s).
baseline: Box (A6000, pace proxy, 5 min): p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024, v13's parent), p4_v0t2 all failed it (0/6). Kaggle L4: 1 of 12 runs (g4-l4-v9-eog, at 308 s). p4_v13 (v13 alone, one sample): failed (box report B-074 and P2_LOG 16:23Z: 0 solved among the first 13 ids, which include this one; trace not yet on the Mac).
regression_risk: The rule adds or changes a step before the first edit. On p4_b1024, 15 of the 28 solved tasks made their first source edit without a failing check before it (MEASURED, fastapi_census.txt section 2); a python check costs 10-17 s of model time per call on the box (docs/forty_two/TIMING.md section 4). Most exposed: rich_3506 and rich_3521 (first source edit at 273 and 270 s, resolved at 304 s through the fallback diff) and fastapi_14458 (resolved at 305 s); an extra call before their edit can push it past the cap. Tasks whose issue has no runnable example (docs-only or wording tasks) may spend a call on a check that cannot be red, and the 'if it passes, change it' clause could cost a second one (INFERRED). Inherits v13's text-call risk (below).
also_applies_to: Any hidden task whose issue gives an example that can be asserted through the public API. Outside the 42: fastapi_11194 and rich_3043 were solved on p4_b1024 with no check before the first edit (the rule fires there; whether it helps or costs time is what the screen of the other 32 will show).
text_call_risk: v13 carries a fenced heredoc block in step 3, suspected in the p4_v13 fastapi_14487 row that wrote every tool call as text (B-074). This bundle inherits that block unchanged; the added sentences have no code fence, no backticks and no tool-call syntax (tested). The leak predates v13: 5 of 1,783 replies on p4_b1024 (fastapi_14487 among them), 1 on p4_v0t2, 3 on p4, 1 on p4_v7, all recovered after the nudge (MEASURED: scripts/forty_two/text_call_leaks.py, fastapi_census.txt section 3). Read the queue run's traces for zero-call rows before reading its score.
